newsitem.title: CHINA: China jails "princeling" for 12 yrs for corruption.
newsitem.headline: China jails "princeling" for 12 yrs for corruption.

text.p: China has sentenced the high-flying son of the disgraced former Beijing Communist Party chief to 12 years in prison for corruption, officials said on Tuesday.

The Chinese capital's Number One Intermediate People's Court convicted Chen Xiaotong, son of former Beijing party boss and Politburo member Chen Xitong, of taking bribes and misusing public funds on June 28, a court spokesman said.
"He was sentenced to six years for taking bribes and seven years for misuse of public funds and the final sentence was 12 years' imprisonment," the spokesman said.
The son of the man who ruled China's capital for more than a decade had not appealed the sentence and had already begun serving his prison term, he said.

The spokesman refused to comment on whether Chinese authorities planned to press charges against Chen Xitong, purged in April 1995 after a multi-million dollar corruption scandal rocked the Chinese capital.
Chen Xiaotong, former president of a Sino-Japanese joint venture hotel in Beijing, the New Century Hotel, was detained in April 1995 for economic irregularities.

Chinese sources said Chen Xiaotong had been held at the Qincheng prison in Beijing's northern suburbs prior to his trial -- the same prison in which China held most of its most prominent dissidents after the 1989 crackdown on pro-democracy demonstrations centred in Tiananmen Square.
Chen Xiaotong is the second princeling -- a sobriquet applied to sons and daughters of China's ruling communist elite -- to be sentenced in a campaign to crack down on corruption.

Zhou Beifang, head of two Hong Kong-listed subsidiaries of Beijing's largest steelworks, Capital Iron and Steel (Shougang), was sentenced last year to a suspended death sentence for graft. His father, Zhou Guanwu, headed the steelworks and was reportedly an associate of late paramount leader Deng Xiaoping.
The Beijing scandal broke in April 1995 when Vice Mayor Wang Baosen committed suicide on a rural hillside after coming under investigation in a $37 million corruption scandal.

Chen Xitong, who ran Beijing for 12 years, first as mayor and then as party secretary, stepped down and was purged from the Politburo, becoming the most senior official to fall in a corruption scandal since the 1949 communist takeover.
Unpublished party documents circulated internally said Chen Xitong abused his office by amassing $24 million in unauthorised funds and lavished favours on friends, associates and a mistress.

Chen Xiaotong illegally channelled government funds to his father's mistress, He Ping, the documents said. He also tipped off his father's mistress about the vice-mayor's suicide and told her to flee to Hong Kong.
Beijing Vice Mayor Zhang Baifa confirmed earlier this year that the younger Chen had been held on corruption charges but said his father's mistress was still on the run.
Zhang said the former Beijing party chief could face punishment for dereliction of duty but not for any more serious offence. Chen has not been seen in public since his disgrace.

Chinese Communist Party chief and state president Jiang Zemin has identified corruption as a virus that could topple the ruling party and has made a crackdown on graft a major plank in his political platform.
